items.response: That error usually means the docker CLI is still pointed at the old Docker Desktop socket (a leftover DOCKER_HOST or a stale docker context), so it never reaches OrbStack. I'd rather check than guess which one it is here. Action: run `docker context ls` and `echo $DOCKER_HOST`, switch to the OrbStack context (or unset the override), then retry `docker compose up`.

There is a real difference. `structuredClone` keeps Dates, Maps, Sets, typed arrays, `undefined` and circular references, while the JSON round-trip turns Dates into strings, drops `undefined` and functions, empties Maps/Sets and throws on cycles. Neither copies functions or class prototypes, and `structuredClone` is available on Node 18, so it is safe for us. Action: keep waiting on the two background checks (Node 20+ APIs, engines.node) and report when they finish.

Action: read the existing worker job and queue conventions and the orgs schema, then add the job plus tests for missing URL, non-2xx and timeout.

The digest is the hash Next attaches to errors in production, and it isn't sent to Sentry automatically, so it needs to be passed explicitly when global-error.tsx reports. It's safe to send because it's only the hash, not the message. Action: read app/global-error.tsx and its Sentry call, add `error.digest` as a searchable tag and as extra data, using ESM imports only, and add a test if there is one for that file.

I'll draft the reply asking for the full error text and `node --version`, since there's no output, and the likely fix is: our CLI is ESM-only, so an old Node fails (often ERR_REQUIRE_ESM); upgrade to Node 18+ and reinstall with `npm i -g @acme/cli`. For the startup check, because ESM can fail at import time on a very old runtime, the entry file should do the version check first with no imports, print a colored warning (plain ANSI, no dependency) and exit, then dynamically import the real main. I'll also add an `engines` field to the CLI package.json, which was suggested but never added. Action: write the draft reply and implement the runtime check with a test that stubs process.versions.
